era: Dreamcast / PS2 / HD ports / VR rhythm
summary: Sega's Ulala-led rhythm-action series, spanning Dreamcast/PS2 cinematic rhythm games and a later VR revival.

entries.title: Space Channel 5

emulation.notes: Dreamcast emulation is the cleanest capture route for the original game.

primary.why: The Dreamcast original is the best main route for the first Space Channel 5: it is the lead version, while the PS2 port came later and the GBA conversion is technically compromised by handheld limits.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Dreamcast version on original hardware or through Flycast/Redream for clean capture. Use the PS2 port only for comparison and the GBA port only as a curiosity.

entries.remaster_caveats: No official HD version of the first game is documented; the GBA conversion is a compromised portable adaptation.

entries.title: Space Channel 5: Part 2

emulation.emulator: Native PC; Flycast/Redream or PCSX2 for original-version fallback
emulation.notes: Use PC HD if owned; otherwise use HD console ports or emulate Dreamcast/PS2.

primary.why: Part 2 received a high-definition port on Windows, Xbox 360, and PS3 in 2011; the Windows version is the highest-fidelity and most capture-friendly route when already owned.
primary.how_to_play: Play the owned Windows PC HD version if available, applying compatibility fixes as needed. If the delisted PC version is unavailable, use the PS3/Xbox 360 HD port or emulate Dreamcast/PS2 as fallback.

entries.remaster_caveats: The PC HD version is delisted on Steam as of December 6, 2024; use already-owned PC copies or the PS3/Xbox 360 HD ports if access is the deciding factor.

entries.title: Space Channel 5 VR: Kinda Funky News Flash
entries.definitive_edition: SteamVR release with Hatsune Miku DLC

emulation.notes: Use a PC VR headset and OBS capture path suited to VR mirroring.

primary.why: The Windows/SteamVR release is the highest-fidelity VR route and launched with the Hatsune Miku DLC bundled, while the earlier PSVR release received that DLC separately.
primary.how_to_play: Play the SteamVR version on PC VR hardware for the main run. Use Quest only for standalone convenience or PSVR only if that is the available headset path.

entries.remaster_caveats: This is a new VR spin-off rather than a remaster of the Dreamcast/PS2 games; PSVR received the Miku DLC separately.
